pre_registered_claim.C: Eccentric (lengthening) muscle actions cause greater force loss, CK/myoglobin efflux, and DOMS than concentric actions performed at matched-or-lower force and substantially (4-5x) lower metabolic cost; the damage driver is fiber-level mechanical STRAIN specifically into the region where the length-tension curve's slope dF/dL turns negative (sarcomere-population instability, 'popping'), not force magnitude or energy expenditure. A single eccentric bout induces a repeated-bout protective adaptation -- structurally linked to an increase in serial sarcomere number -- that reduces second-bout damage markers by a large margin and persists 6-9 months before being lost by 12 months. Exertional rhabdomyolysis sits on the SAME continuum as ordinary EIMD, not a qualitatively separate process, and CK magnitude alone does not cleanly separate benign exercise-induced elevation from clinically dangerous rhabdomyolysis.
pre_registered_claim.not_C: (a) Damage scales with the metabolic/energetic cost of the contraction or with force magnitude, not strain -- so a lower-energy-cost, similar/lower-force contraction (eccentric) should show LESS OR EQUAL damage to concentric, never more. (b) The repeated-bout effect is a short-lived (days), non-specific 'warm-up'/generic-conditioning artifact rather than a structurally-grounded, durable, largely eccentric-specific adaptation. (c) A clean CK threshold reliably separates benign EIMD from dangerous rhabdomyolysis/AKI risk.
pre_registered_claim.threshold_preregistered: F1 (strain not force/energy): >=2 independent decorrelated human studies must show eccentric damage markers exceeding concentric at matched-or-lower force AND >=2x lower metabolic cost -- else not_C(a) stands. F2 (RBE real+durable): a 2nd eccentric bout must show materially reduced CK and/or attenuated force loss in >=2 independent studies, with protection demonstrated to survive to >=1 month in a dedicated duration study -- if protection is absent within days or statistically indistinguishable from a non-eccentric prior-bout control, not_C(b) stands. F3 (no clean CK/AKI threshold): if one CK cutoff cleanly partitions AKI vs non-AKI or benign-vs-hospitalized cases across a systematic review + a real case series, not_C(c) stands; if ranges overlap substantially, C stands.
pre_registered_claim.adversary_forced: (a) The strongest fair form of 'it's just energy/force' is not an unmatched comparison but Isner-Horobeti et al 2013's own explicit MATCHED-MECHANICAL-POWER comparison (identical external force x velocity output, cycle ergometry) -- forced onto its own best, most-controlled terrain, and it still inverts sign (lower cost, more damage). (b) The strongest fair form of 'RBE is generic conditioning' is Nosaka & Clarkson 1997's own finding that a prior CONCENTRIC bout or a mere warm-up DOES partially attenuate subsequent eccentric damage -- retained here as a genuine partial confound, not dismissed; the eccentric-specific literature's larger, more complete, far-longer-lasting (6-9 month) protection is reported as the stronger but not exclusive effect. (c) The strongest fair form of 'CK predicts rhabdo severity' is tested against the largest available systematic review of RML definitions (614 papers screened) and a real n=30 hospitalized case series reporting its full admission-CK range, not a cherry-picked cutoff.

evidence.cite: Newham DJ, Mills KR, Quigley BM, Edwards RH. Pain and fatigue after concentric and eccentric muscle contractions. Clin Sci (Lond). 1983;64(1):55-62.
evidence.n: normal subjects, bilateral step test (1 leg concentric, contralateral leg eccentric, SAME task/session)
evidence.value: Force and force-frequency changes were greater in the eccentrically-contracted leg; pain/tenderness developed ONLY in the eccentric leg (onset ~8h, peak ~48h); EMG showed increased electrical activation only in the eccentric leg. Authors' own conclusion, quoted: 'These changes cannot be explained in simple metabolic terms...the result of mechanical trauma caused by the high tension generated in relatively few active fibres during eccentric contractions.'

evidence.cite: Isner-Horobeti ME, Dufour SP, Vautravers P, Geny B, Coudeyre E, Richard R. Eccentric exercise training: modalities, applications and perspectives. Sports Med. 2013;43(6):483-512.

J Physiol. 1952;117(3):380-90 (PMID 14946742, PMC1392548, DOI 10.1113/jphysiol.1952.sp004755) and its follow-up Abbott BC, Bigland B. falsifier_tests.measure: sarcomere-string mechanical model + direct causal animal test of its own prediction

evidence.cite: Morgan DL. New insights into the behavior of muscle during active lengthening. Biophys J. 1990;57(2):209-21.
evidence.n: sarcomere-string Hill-type simulation w/ random inter-sarcomere variation

Explains permanent extra tension after stretch on the descending limb and continued tension rise during continued stretch.

evidence.cite: Morgan DL, Proske U. Sarcomere popping requires stretch over a range where total tension decreases with length. J Physiol. 2006;574(Pt 2):627-8.
evidence.value: Formal restatement of the instability criterion: popping requires dF/dL<0 (descending-limb) over the stretch range.

evidence.cite: Lynn R, Morgan DL. Decline running produces more sarcomeres in rat vastus intermedius muscle fibers than does incline running. J Appl Physiol. 1994;77(3):1439-44.
evidence.n: rat treadmill, 16-degree incline vs decline, VI muscle fiber/sarcomere-length digestion assay
evidence.value: DIRECT causal test of Morgan (1990)'s own prediction: decline (eccentric-biased) running produced significantly MORE sarcomeres in series per fiber than incline (concentric-biased) running -- confirmed, not merely proposed.

evidence.cite: Lynn R, Talbot JA, Morgan DL. Differences in rat skeletal muscles after incline and decline running. J Appl Physiol. 1998;85(1):98-104.
evidence.n: rat treadmill training + standardized post-training eccentric-contraction damage test
evidence.value: Decline-trained (more-serial-sarcomere) muscles showed LESS torque fall and LESS optimum-angle shift after a standardized series of lengthening contractions than incline-trained muscles -- i.e., the measured structural adaptation (more sarcomeres in series) is directly linked, in the SAME study, to measured functional protection.

evidence.cite: Butterfield TA, Leonard TR, Herzog W. Differential serial sarcomere number adaptations in knee extensor muscles of rats is contraction type dependent. J Appl Physiol. 2005;99(4):1352-8.
evidence.n: rat VL/VI, chronic incline vs decline training
evidence.value: Bidirectional, independent confirmation: short (concentric-biased) operating lengths -> LOSS of serial sarcomeres; long (eccentric-biased) operating lengths -> GAIN of serial sarcomeres.

falsifier_tests.note: GEOMETRIC DERIVATION (not a heuristic): sarcomeres in series share one common instantaneous tension (an exact mechanical-equilibrium constraint). On the ascending limb/plateau (dF/dL>=0), a momentarily-weak sarcomere lengthening toward the common tension INCREASES its own force -- negative feedback, stable, strain distributes evenly. On the descending limb (dF/dL<0), the same weak sarcomere lengthening to try to reach the common tension DECREASES its force further -- positive feedback, runaway ('pop') until filament overlap is lost and passive elements bear the load, while neighboring sarcomeres barely lengthen at all (they absorbed almost none of the imposed excursion). This is a stability argument on the sign of a local slope (dF/dL), structurally identical in form to a negative-eigenvalue/negative-stiffness instability criterion. It explains, from the SAME geometric fact, both why eccentric lengthening at long/stretched lengths concentrates damage in a minority of fibers/sarcomeres (Brooks 1995's 'high tension in relatively few active fibres', Newham 1983) AND why the adaptation is sarcomerogenesis: adding sarcomeres in series divides a fixed fascicle-level excursion across more units, reducing per-sarcomere strain and pushing the population away from the unstable dF/dL<0 zone -- independently, causally confirmed in the SAME rat preparation (Lynn/Talbot/Morgan 1998).

Cellular evidence: longitudinal addition of sarcomeres in series (reduces per-sarcomere strain, directly consistent with F3's geometric mechanism) + a blunted secondary inflammatory response.

falsifier_tests.verdict: PARTIAL (forced, disclosed, not swept aside -- the adversary is not fully defeated, only shown to be the weaker of two real effects)
falsifier_tests.measure: prior CONCENTRIC/warm-up exposure vs prior ECCENTRIC exposure as the protective trigger; effect of an inter-bout gap too short for recovery

evidence.cite: Nosaka K, Clarkson PM. Influence of previous concentric exercise on eccentric exercise-induced muscle damage. J Sports Sci. 1997;15(5):477-83.
evidence.value: A prior bout of 100 CONCENTRIC-only elbow-flexor contractions (CON-ECC condition) produced LOWER soreness, FASTER force recovery, and SMALLER CK rise on a subsequent eccentric bout than eccentric alone (ECC condition), 2 weeks apart. A separate n=5 experiment: plain warm-up exercise before the eccentric bout ALSO attenuated damage.

evidence.cite: Paddon-Jones D, Muthalib M, Jenkins D. The effects of a repeated bout of eccentric exercise on indices of muscle damage and delayed onset muscle soreness. J Sci Med Sport. 2000;3(1):35-43.
evidence.value: Repeating the SAME maximal eccentric bout only 2 DAYS later (before recovery from bout 1) produced a FURTHER acute impairment in isometric torque (-30+/-5%) and flexed elbow angle (-20+/-4%), even though subjects produced uniformly LOWER work/torque during bout 2 -- i.e. re-exposure before recovery is completed does NOT show protection; the recovery time course was not accelerated either.

falsifier_tests.note: Symmetric QC on the RBE claim itself. (a) The 'it's just generic conditioning, not eccentric-specific' adversary is FORCED to its strongest form (a real prior-CONCENTRIC-bout control, not a strawman) and is NOT cleanly defeated -- concentric/warm-up exposure gives real, partial protection. What survives is a DIFFERENCE OF DEGREE: F4's eccentric-specific protection is far larger (near-complete CK/Mb abolition) and far more durable (6-9 months, Nosaka 2001) than anything reported for non-eccentric priming in this literature, but the concentric/warm-up confound is disclosed, not hidden. (b) A genuine, non-monotonic TIMING boundary exists: P(protection) is NOT simply 'more elapsed time is always better before it decays' -- at Delta t=2 days (before repair has progressed), a second bout is WORSE, not better, than exposure alone. The protective state must be triggered by a repair process that has not yet run, not by mere elapsed clock time.

Both papers report serum CK activity in the same U/L(=IU/L) clinical-chemistry unit, so this is a valid same-unit comparison, not a units artifact. falsifier_tests.measure: cell-population-specific response to eccentrically-biased exercise damage

evidence.cite: Parise G, McKinnell IW, Rudnicki MA. Muscle satellite cell and atypical myogenic progenitor response following exercise. Muscle Nerve. 2008;37(5):611-9.

falsifier_tests.note: Couples this doc directly to the task's named satellite-cell/regeneration axis: the human histological timecourse (biopsy, days-to-weeks) and the mouse cell-population timecourse (flow/immunohistochemistry, hours-to-days) are DECORRELATED methods/species/timescales that agree on ORDER: acute mechanical injury -> biomarker efflux (days 1-6) -> immune/satellite-cell response (peaks 2-4 days, sustained ~1-4 days beyond that) -> regeneration (by ~3 weeks). No satellite-cell/regeneration MECHANISM doc exists yet in this repo (checked by directory listing before writing this doc) -- this is a first, not a duplicate.

geometric_mechanism.derivation: Sarcomeres within one myofibril are mechanically in SERIES: at any instant they all carry the identical tension T (an exact equilibrium constraint, not an approximation), while their individual lengths L_i can differ. Let F_i(L_i) be sarcomere i's active force-length function -- ascending on the actin-myosin-overlap-increasing side, flat at the plateau (maximal overlap), then descending as overlap is lost beyond optimal length. If sarcomere k is transiently the weakest (natural biological variance) and the whole fiber is stretched, equilibrium requires L_k to shift until F_k(L_k)=T. On the ascending limb/plateau, dF/dL>=0: as L_k increases toward the common T, F_k RISES toward T -- negative feedback, a stable, self-limiting distribution of the imposed stretch across all sarcomeres. On the descending limb, dF/dL<0: as L_k increases toward the (higher) common T, F_k instead FALLS further below T -- positive feedback, a runaway ('pop') that only stops when L_k exceeds filament overlap entirely and passive structural elements (titin, connective tissue) take over the load, while the OTHER, stronger sarcomeres barely lengthen at all because the popped sarcomere absorbed almost the entire imposed excursion. This is a stability argument on the SIGN of a local slope (dF/dL), the same structural form as a negative-eigenvalue/negative-differential-stiffness instability criterion in any series-coupled mechanical system -- not a heuristic, and not specific to muscle.
geometric_mechanism.consequence: The SAME geometric fact explains, without a separate free parameter: (1) why damage is a strain (not force, not energy) phenomenon -- F2's Lieber/Fridén result and F1's Newham/Isner-Horobeti result are two independent, decorrelated confirmations of a single underlying instability criterion; (2) why damage concentrates in a MINORITY of fibers/sarcomeres under high tension (Brooks 1995's 'high tension in relatively few active fibres'), because popping is a discrete, one-at-a-time, weakest-first event, not a uniform strain applied to every sarcomere equally; (3) why the repeated-bout adaptation is (in significant part) sarcomerogenesis: adding sarcomeres in series divides a FIXED fascicle-level excursion across more units (per-sarcomere strain ~ DeltaL_fascicle / N), pushing the whole population away from the dF/dL<0 instability zone for the SAME external movement -- independently, causally confirmed in the SAME rat preparation (F3, Lynn/Talbot/Morgan 1998: more sarcomeres in series -> measurably less torque fall on a standardized subsequent eccentric challenge).

quantitative_timecourse_model.form: Two dose-dependent REGIMES (not a single universal curve -- an honestly disclosed, non-monotone-across-severity structure, not false precision), each anchored to explicit literature landmarks; both regimes share the same qualitative sequence (mechanical injury at t=0 -> biomarker efflux delayed 24-48h -> peak biomarker/soreness days 1-6 -> satellite-cell response peaks ~48h, sustained to ~96h -> histological regeneration signs by ~3 weeks) but differ sharply in MAGNITUDE and total RECOVERY time.

landmarks.state: pain/DOMS peak; force generation and EMG activation had ALREADY returned to pre-exercise baseline at this same timepoint -- i.e. for this mild dose, functional recovery precedes/coincides with the pain peak, not after it

regime_maximal_unaccustomed.example_protocol: maximal/near-maximal unaccustomed eccentric contractions, elbow flexors or multi-muscle whole-body protocols (Nosaka/Clarkson/Chen lineage)

MVC still depressed 13-49%; DOMS rising toward peak (43-70mm on the cited visual-analogue scale)
CK/myoglobin/AST/LDH/ALT all BELOW detection of a significant rise -- a genuine reporting-delay window, not absence of injury

CK/myoglobin/AST/LDH/ALT peak (myoglobin/AST/LDH/ALT follow CK's own time course but at lower absolute peak); CK peak magnitude highly protocol/individual dependent, spanning roughly 2 orders of magnitude across cited cohorts: 6,740-24,200 U/L (single-limb forearm-flexor protocol) to 23,238-207,304 IU/L (9-muscle whole-body protocol)

quantitative_timecourse_model.why_two_regimes_not_one: This is a forced, disclosed dose-response structure, not an inconsistency swept aside: the SAME measured quantities (force loss magnitude, CK peak, recovery time) span roughly an order of magnitude or more between the mild and maximal regimes across the cited studies. Treating EIMD timing/magnitude as protocol-intensity- and muscle-mass-dependent is itself falsifiable (a specific protocol's dose predicts which regime it falls in) and is the honest alternative to fitting one curve that would fit neither regime well.

repeated_bout_protection_model.form: P(delta_t) in [0,1], a protection FACTOR that multiplies the same strain-driven damage_rate a second bout would otherwise produce; anchored at 5 independent, real inter-bout-interval datapoints across 3 decorrelated studies -- NOT a fitted continuous curve (the functional form between anchors, e.g. at 2-3 months, was not tested by any located study and is NOT interpolated here as a number).

near-complete for biomarkers (CK/Mb do not rise significantly at all on bout 2, 9/9 muscle groups); large and significant for force-loss/DOMS but not fully abolished

present but AGE-MODULATED completeness: full protection across all measures in young men; in old men, protection demonstrated ONLY for ROM/myoglobin/soreness, NOT for isometric strength/CK/limb circumference
still present for most measures (faster MIF recovery, reduced soreness, smaller CK/circumference/MRI-T2 rise)
still present for most measures except range-of-motion
ABSENT -- no significant repeated-bout effect on any measure

repeated_bout_protection_model.cross_species_convergence_flagged_not_co: The human duration/magnitude curve above (serum biomarkers + subjective soreness + strength) and the rat structural mechanism (F3: serial sarcomere number, causally linked to measured torque protection) are DECORRELATED bodies of evidence (different species, different measurement modality) that converge DIRECTIONALLY -- both show a real, large, structurally-plausible protective adaptation -- but no single cited study bridges both in one preparation; presented as mutually reinforcing, not as one experiment.

dysfunction_pole_exertional_rhabdomyolys.claim: Exertional rhabdomyolysis is the same mechanical-strain-driven injury process pushed to an extreme, complicated in a minority of cases by acute kidney injury; there is no validated bright-line CK cutoff, per F6.
dysfunction_pole_exertional_rhabdomyolys.graded_continuum_evidence_summary: Benign, non-hospitalized research-protocol CK peaks span 6,740-207,304 U/L across cited healthy-volunteer cohorts (PMID 1740632, 30663816); hospitalized exertional-rhabdomyolysis case-series CK spans 697-233,180 U/L (PMID 25643388) -- the ranges OVERLAP almost entirely rather than being cleanly separated, and only 20% of the hospitalized case series had any AKI evidence at all, with higher creatinine correlating to LOWER (not higher) CK in that same series.
dysfunction_pole_exertional_rhabdomyolys.additional_criteria_required: Per the systematic review (PMID 30617905): clinical syndrome (weakness, myalgia, muscle swelling) + CK>1000 IU/L or >5xULN for a 'mild' designation; ADDITIONALLY myoglobinuria + measured AKI for 'severe'. CK number alone is necessary but not remotely sufficient.

aging.cite: Lavender AP, Nosaka K. Responses of old men to repeated bouts of eccentric exercise of the elbow flexors in comparison with young men. Eur J Appl Physiol. 2006;97(5):619-26.
aging.measured: Old men (70.5+/-4.1y) showed SMALLER first-bout damage than young men (20.4+/-2.0y) across all measures, but also an INCOMPLETE repeated-bout effect (protection only for ROM/myoglobin/soreness, not strength/CK/circumference) at a 4-week gap.
aging.cross_check_rat_structural: Hinks A, Patterson MA, Njai BS, Power GA. Age-related blunting of serial sarcomerogenesis and mechanical adaptations following 4 wk of maximal eccentric resistance training. J Appl Physiol. 2024;136(5):1209-25 (PMID 38511212, DOI 10.1152/japplphysiol.00041.2024, fetched live): the SAME 4-week maximal eccentric training stimulus that INCREASED serial sarcomere number and improved performance in young rats caused NO serial-sarcomere increase in soleus and an outright LOSS of serial sarcomeres in lateral gastrocnemius in old rats, with reduced max torque/velocity/power and increased passive torque -- 'dysfunctional remodeling' in the paper's own words. Disclosed as directionally convergent with, but methodologically separate from (different species/paradigm), the human aging-RBE finding above -- not conflated as one experiment.
aging.dysfunction_reading: This is a candidate mechanism for why the SAME nominal training stimulus is adaptive (FUNCTION pole) in young tissue and can become maladaptive (DYSFUNCTION pole, a genuine sign-flip not just an attenuated magnitude) in old tissue -- directly relevant to this twin's function-vs-dysfunction organizing axis for training prescription in older individuals.

sex_difference.cite: Clarkson PM, Hubal MJ. Exercise-induced muscle damage in humans. Am J Phys Med Rehabil. 2002;81(11 Suppl):S52-69.
sex_difference.measured: Explicitly flagged by the review itself as CONTROVERSIAL/unresolved: animal literature clearly shows females sustain less eccentric damage than males; human literature shows either no sex difference or the OPPOSITE (women more susceptible). Not resolved by this synthesis -- an open question in the primary literature, disclosed as such, not silently picked one way.

trained_repeated_exposure_as_the_athlete.cite: Balnave CD, Thompson MW. Effect of training on eccentric exercise-induced muscle damage. J Appl Physiol. 1993;75(4):1545-51.
trained_repeated_exposure_as_the_athlete.measured: 8 weeks of once-weekly eccentric-downhill-walk training progressively reduced DOMS, serum CK/myoglobin response, and functional (MVC/fatigability) impairment -- BUT on genuinely DIFFERENT time courses for each marker; authors' own conclusion: 'the function of the muscle can be impaired without apparent muscle damage' (a real, disclosed dissociation between biomarker-adaptation and function-adaptation, not a single monolithic 'adaptation' variable).
trained_repeated_exposure_as_the_athlete.framing: The trained-athlete's resistance to EIMD is read here as the SAME repeated-bout-effect mechanism (F3/F4) operating continuously across a training history, rather than a separate phenomenon -- a within-subject, repeated-exposure design (this study; also Lynn/Talbot/Morgan 1998's trained-vs-untrained rats) is used in preference to a cross-sectional elite-vs-untrained human comparison specifically because within-subject designs remove the self-selection confound a cross-sectional comparison could not (disclosed as a deliberate methodological choice in honest_gaps).

honest_gaps: No new raw simulation/code was executed this pass -- this is a literature-forced quantitative/geometric model (an explicit stability-criterion derivation + real anchored parameter values), status OPEN; the actual numeric integrator (a repair/recovery ODE + the P(delta_t) protection state, added to the sibling muscle_damage.py's existing monotone accumulator) is PROPOSED (see proposed_cell), not built or run, here.

Sarcomere length-tension numeric landmarks (exact ascending/plateau/descending-limb boundary values, e.g. in micrometers) were NOT re-derived or re-verified this session -- the dF/dL-sign STABILITY ARGUMENT is solid and directly sourced (Morgan 1990/2006), but computing this twin's own specific per-sarcomere strain threshold from its deployed Millard2012EquilibriumMuscle force-length curve was not attempted here; a pointer, not a duplication, of docs/MECHANISM_CROSSBRIDGE_MODEL.md / docs/MECHANISM_SPECIFIC_TENSION.md / the sibling MECHANISM_MUSCLE_DAMAGE.md's own whole-fiber 30%-strain Brooks-threshold section.

The exact PERCENTAGE increase in serial sarcomere number from eccentric training was not extracted from the cited rat studies (Lynn/Morgan 1994, Lynn/Talbot/Morgan 1998, Butterfield 2005, Hinks 2024) -- their abstracts report DIRECTION and statistical significance, not the specific magnitude; full-text/table numbers were not fetched this pass.

The causal sarcomerogenesis-directly-linked-to-protection chain (F3, Lynn/Talbot/Morgan 1998) is RAT vastus intermedius; the human RBE duration/magnitude data (F4/F5, Nosaka/Chen/Clarkson lineage) is a separate, decorrelated (human, serum-biomarker/subjective-soreness) body of evidence. The two converge directionally and are presented as mutually reinforcing -- no single cited study bridges both in one species/preparation.

F6's headline cross-study CK-range overlap (Chen 2019 healthy-volunteer max 207,304 IU/L vs Oh 2015 hospitalized-rhabdomyolysis range 697-233,180 U/L) was COMPUTED here by comparing two independently published ranges; neither source paper makes this comparison itself, and Chen et al report no renal-function/clinical-outcome data for their volunteers -- a valid number-vs-number cross-check, not a claim that those specific research subjects had clinical rhabdomyolysis.

Clarkson et al 1986 (PMID 3733311) found CK rose EQUALLY (~34-38%) across eccentric/concentric/isometric protocols matched for work-time/work-rest ratio at a SUBMAXIMAL intensity in untrained women, even though soreness still showed the expected eccentric-and-isometric-greater-than-concentric asymmetry in the SAME dataset -- a genuine, disclosed dose-dependent boundary: the large eccentric-specific CK differential (F1, F4) is robust at MAXIMAL/unaccustomed intensities but the authors' own submaximal, matched-duration protocol did not reproduce it in the CK channel specifically (their own stated conclusion: at this dose 'the increase in serum CK activity may not provide a sensitive indicator of the magnitude of injury'). Forced via OODA (checked: is this a refutation of the whole claim, or a regime boundary? Answer: a regime boundary -- the soreness marker in the SAME dataset still shows the predicted asymmetry), not swept aside.
Sex-difference in EIMD susceptibility is explicitly flagged by Clarkson & Hubal (2002) themselves as unresolved/contradictory in humans -- not adjudicated here.

DOMS' proximate PAIN-GENERATION mechanism (the nociceptor-sensitization pathway/mediator) is, per Newham's own 1988 review (PMID 3371343), NOT explained by any of the measured damage/inflammation/intramuscular-pressure time courses (all differ from the pain's own time course), and anti-inflammatory drugs do not relieve the pain. This doc models damage-MARKER kinetics (force, CK, satellite cells) quantitatively; the pain-generation mechanism itself remains an open question in the primary literature, not resolved by this synthesis.

The 'trained resists more' claim is evidenced here via WITHIN-SUBJECT repeated-exposure/training designs (Balnave & Thompson 1993 human; Lynn/Talbot/Morgan 1998 rat) rather than a cross-sectional elite-athlete-vs-untrained-control single-timepoint human comparison -- a deliberate choice (avoids a self-selection confound) but means no such cross-sectional human study was searched for or found this pass. The special-ops CK data (Shumway 2020) describes TRAINEES/candidates during selection, not already-elite veterans -- read as suggestive, not as a direct trained-vs-untrained test.

All numbers in this document were extracted from PubMed abstract TEXT via NCBI eutils (esearch/esummary/efetch), live this session -- no figure was viewed or eyeballed for any quantitative claim; several full-text/table-only numbers (exact SSN percentage changes, the classic Abbott/Bigland/Ritchie 1952/1953 O2-cost ratio itself) were explicitly NOT available via abstract and are flagged above rather than invented.
proposed_cell: Extend scripts/msk/muscle_damage.py (currently, by its own explicit design, a MONOTONE non-recovering single-bout accumulator) with: (1) a REPAIR/RECOVERY term on the existing damage state, parametrized by the two dose-dependent regimes anchored above (~24-48h for a mild/submaximal episode per Newham 1983; ~7-10 days for a maximal/unaccustomed episode per the Nosaka/Clarkson/Chen lineage); (2) a REPEATED-BOUT protection state variable P(delta_t) multiplying damage_rate before accumulation, anchored at this doc's own 6 real data points (~0 or negative at 2 days, near-complete for biomarkers by 2 weeks, still-present at 6-9 months, gone by 12 months); (3) an AGING modulator on P(delta_t) informed by both the human (Lavender & Nosaka 2006) and the rat structural (Hinks 2024) findings, including the possibility of a SIGN FLIP (not just attenuation) at old age + maximal dose. Pre-registered decisive gate for the next session that builds this: apply the resulting model to this twin's OWN already-measured DJ1 drop-landing episode (sibling cert, Section 8: peak eccentric v_norm up to 1.43, 1.9-8.6x walking's own peak, already on disk, zero new data acquisition needed) as a synthetic 'bout 1', then check whether a simulated 'bout 2' at the SAME kinematics produces a measurably lower accumulated damage state after the P(delta_t) term is applied -- a cheap, decisive, fully machine-checkable OODA test using data already in this repo, not requiring any new mocap/EMG/blood-draw acquisition.
